covers: design 18.2: the code block font size
items.question: What font size does a code block draw in? Nothing in app.css sets it.
items.answer: 13px, family `monospace`, line height 18.2px (1.4 x 13). CodeMirror's base theme sets `font-family: monospace` on .cm-scroller and nothing sets a size, so Chromium's default fixed font size (13px) applies instead of the editor's 16px. The same 13px shows in the Markdown and Typst code blocks. .cm-content has padding 4px 0 and .cm-line padding 0 2px (the view theme override at cmview.svelte.ts:159); a monospace character advances 7.828125px. The inline chip draws in the paragraph's face (system-ui 17.072px) and the raw block island in the body face (markdown raw block system-ui 16px, app.css:1984-1996 inherits it). A canvas code block needs the engine's default fixed size per platform (13px on Chromium everywhere) as a style table entry, not 16px.

evidence.method: getComputedStyle of .cm-content, .cm-line and .cm-scroller in the running DOM editor, three dialects

covers: design 18.2: whether read-only blocks typing in an island
items.question: When the editor is read-only, does a CodeMirror island still take typing?
items.answer: Yes. With ProseMirror's editable prop false, a typed key still went into the code block: CodeMirror's first line changed from "  d ef f(x):" to " Q d ef f(x):" and ProseMirror's code_block text followed (" Q d ef f(x):"). The island's .cm-content stays contenteditable=true, CodeMirror's readOnly facet is false and ProseMirror does not refuse the forwarded transaction. Only the gear is disabled. The app cannot reach this state offline (isReadOnly is a constant false in permissionStore.ts:4-8), so the canvas decides: it refuses input to islands when the editor is not editable.

evidence.method: view.setProps({ editable: () => false }) in the running DOM editor, click into the code block, type Q, read both documents

items.question: What does the disabled code block gear look like?
items.answer: Opacity 0.5 and nothing else: cursor stays pointer, color and border do not change (Skeleton's :disabled rule). Measured by setting disabled on the gear button, because the state cannot occur offline.

evidence.method: getComputedStyle of the gear before and after setting disabled

covers: design 18.2: whether peer carets draw inside islands today
items.question: Do a peer's caret and selection draw inside a code block, raw block or inline chip today?
items.answer: No. A peer fed through the plugin's own channel (a remote-cursors meta with positions inside each node) drew a caret and a selection tint in a paragraph and nothing inside a code block, an inline chip or an open raw block, in LaTeX, Markdown and Typst. remoteCursors.ts draws widgets and decorations at ProseMirror positions, and a node view with CodeMirror inside has no content DOM for them to land in. A second participant could not run here: a session needs a relay server and a second window, and the repository ships neither. The simulation reaches the same plugin state a real peer reaches through peersOnText (remoteCursors.ts:144), so the drawing answer holds; whether peersOnText maps a real awareness cursor inside a block to a position inside it is read from pmAtOffset (sourceMap.ts:91-104): the fallback returns block.pmFrom + 1, a position inside the node.

evidence.method: setMeta on the remote-cursors plugin key with a peer whose anchor and head lie inside each node kind, then query .pm-remote-caret and .pm-remote-sel

items.question: Which table does the installed @codemirror/commands defaultKeymap hold?
items.answer: @codemirror/commands 6.11.1: 59 bindings (39 of them in standardKeymap), listed in defaultKeymap.json with key, mac, win, linux, run and shift. The 20 extra ones include Mod-Alt-ArrowUp and Mod-Alt-ArrowDown (addCursorAbove, addCursorBelow), so the inventory's doubt is settled: they are in defaultKeymap, and the island mounts [...codeMirrorKeymap(), ...defaultKeymap] then [tabIndentBinding]. completionKeymap (@codemirror/autocomplete 6.20.4) is in the same file. Run names are the exported command names.

evidence.method: imported the installed packages in Node and reverse mapped each run function to its export name

items.question: What are indentUnit and tabSize in an island?
items.answer: tabSize 4 and indentUnit two spaces, both CodeMirror defaults: the app sets neither (the compartment named tabSize in cmview.svelte.ts:65 is never configured). state.tabSize is 4, computed tab-size is 4, and a literal tab advances 31.3125px = 4 x 7.828125px. Tab at the start of "def f(x):" gave "  def f(x):" (two spaces) and Tab at column 3 of that line inserted one space, to the next stop of 2 ("  d ef f(x):"): the indentAtCaret rule in cmTabKey.ts:13-22.

evidence.method: read view.state.tabSize and getComputedStyle, pressed Tab in a code block, measured a literal tab with coordsAtPos

items.question: Does the app-wide 3px transparent right border apply to islands, and what does it do to the wrap width?
items.answer: Yes, on every .cm-scroller. A wrapped inline chip: wrapper 760px wide, scroller border box 760px, client width 757px, .cm-content 757px. The open raw block measures the same (760 to 757px). So the text wraps at the block width minus 3px. A code block does not wrap and scrolls sideways: its scroller is 734px with 731px of client width, so the visible code area is 3px narrower than the wrapper's content box (734px).

evidence.method: getBoundingClientRect, clientWidth and the glyph rects of each .cm-scroller and .cm-content

covers: design 18.2: a wrapped chip's outline shape
items.question: What shape is the focus outline of an inline chip that wraps onto two lines?
items.answer: One rectangle around the whole inline-block (760 x 56px, getClientRects().length = 1), not one per line fragment. The outline is 1px solid color-mix(surface-500 45%, transparent), offset 1px, radius 2px (0.5 x radius-base), on the wrapper through :focus-within; the .cm-editor itself has outline none. The box is as wide as the line and as tall as the lines (2 visual lines of 27.991px).

evidence.method: focused a two line chip, read computed outline and client rects, screenshot at 3x

rawCssRule: .ProseMirror .inline-latex-wrapper:focus-within, .ProseMirror .raw-latex-wrapper:focus-within { outline: var(--default-border-width) solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface-500) 45%, transparent); }

items.question: What does Tab do inside an inline chip?
items.answer: Tab leaves the chip by the browser's focus order: focus moved to the next focusable thing, here the next island's .cm-content (the code block), and ProseMirror's selection moved to 290 (the start of that block). The chip text did not change (no tab indent). Shift+Tab from the chip ended with focus still in the chip and the selection unchanged (33): no earlier focus stop took it out. Tab inside a code block is different: tabIndentBinding indents.

evidence.method: clicked into a chip, pressed Tab and Shift+Tab, described document.activeElement and the PM selection

covers: design 18.2: the page view dark sheet color
items.question: What color is the page view sheet in dark mode?
items.answer: oklch(0.985 0.002 247.839) (oklch 98.5% 0.002 247.839, near white), from --page-sheet: light-dark(#fff, oklch(98.5% 0.002 247.839)) at texpile-default-theme.css:315; light mode paints rgb(255, 255, 255). The sheet's text color in dark mode is oklch(0.9851 0 none) (the dark mode text color) and the first paragraph's is oklch(0.9851 0 none), as light as the sheet, so plain text on the dark sheet is nearly invisible (see the screenshot; only syntax colored text shows). Recorded as measured; the canvas replays the same two colors unless Louis decides otherwise. The mode was set the way theme.ts apply() sets it (data-mode and the dark class on html) and the page-view class the way LatexEditorView.svelte:284 adds it.

evidence.method: toggled data-mode, the dark class and .page-view in the running DOM editor, read computed colors, screenshots

items.question: Is there a CSS rule for .typ-ref?
items.answer: No. None of the 16 readable stylesheets has a selector containing "typ-ref"; the class is only a marker (TypstRefDisplay.svelte:48, refSchema.ts:30), and the look comes from utilities (rounded-base, cursor-pointer, transition-colors, text-ref-fg or text-ref-broken-fg with hover backgrounds, and py-0.5 -my-0.5 for a label ref). Computed on a broken ref: display block (blockified by the inline-flex button parent), padding 0px, radius 4px, cursor pointer.

evidence.method: scanned document.styleSheets cssRules for the selector and read computed style of a .typ-ref

covers: design 18.2: the texpile-template-block rule being dead
items.question: Does anything produce .texpile-template-block?
items.answer: No. app.css:1661 onward holds rules for it (51 selector entries in the loaded sheets, duplicates included) (including a 4px accent border-left that CLAUDE.md forbids), no source file under apps/ or packages/ outside app.css mentions the class, .template-block-label or .template-block-content, and the DOM scans of the LaTeX, Markdown and Typst documents found 0 elements. Dead CSS from the removed template system; the canvas style sheet does not need it.

items.question: Which code reads the .noautofocus class?
items.answer: None. It is assigned to three wrappers (rawLatexView.ts:79, inlineLatexView.ts:55, cmview.svelte.ts:87) and no selector, closest(), classList check or CSS rule anywhere in apps/ or packages/ reads it. A dead marker; the canvas does not need an equivalent.

items.question: Does raw_latex have a lang attribute, and is it re-read when it changes?
items.answer: The base schema's raw_latex has no lang (baseNodes.ts:90-101). Markdown adds lang with default 'latex' (markdown/visual/schema.ts:33-36) and Typst with default 'typst' (typst/visual/schema.ts:51-54). RawLatexView reads it once in its constructor (rawLatexView.ts:55, 84) and update() does not look at it (rawLatexView.ts:239-247), so a changed lang keeps the old language. LaTeX documents get no RawLatexView island on selection: opening a raw chip selection there left no .raw-latex-wrapper (rawBlockInLatex.opened = false), the edit goes through the chip panel (.drawn-chip-panel .cm-content, tests/integration/titleBlock.spec.ts:21).

evidence.method: code reading, plus selecting a raw_latex node in the LaTeX and Markdown documents

items.question: Which of the listed integration specs run in the visual editor and which in the source editor?
items.answer: Visual editor (VisualEditor driver, .ProseMirror): chipsAndMath, caretWalk, macroArguments, visualFind, undoScroll. Visual editor opening a chip panel whose CodeMirror is the panel's own (.drawn-chip-panel .cm-content): bibliography, titleBlock. Both editors, switching modes and checking the file on disk: visualEditor. Source editor only (SourceEditor driver, sourceCmView): keyboardShortcuts, completionTyping, completionBib.

evidence.method: read each spec's imports and locators
